title: An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone
main_claim: The hyperbolicity cone K of p(X,Z,y)=det((det X)Z − Φ_y(adj X)) in 23 variables, which the companion paper shows is not spectrahedral, is a spectrahedral shadow. It is the exact projection of a homogeneous 100×100 pencil with 307 auxiliary variables (a degree-7 trigonometric moment functional tested against degree-2 trigonometric vectors). The equivalence holds on the whole closed cone, including singular X.
coverage:
I read every section: intro, slices/angular, matching and lift. I checked these numerically with python, to about 1e-13 on random instances:
- Lemma 2.1, the angular Gram factorization of Q.
- Identity (Phi-factor), Φ_y(W)=Σ B(r_j)^T W B(r_j).
- det L_θ = p on each slice (Lemma 2.2).
- Lemma 3.1, the degree-two matching identity. I built C(θ)=R0·M(θ) exactly as the paper specifies and confirmed that C̃C̃^T=Q(z), that ⟨F_θ,C⟩_S = tr(S Q(Y_θ,z)) for random indefinite S, and that C has only Fourier frequencies −2, 0 and 2.

I also checked by hand:
- The frequency-reduction step and the value-plus-derivative argument.
- The block computations in the converse of Prop 4.1. Constant top-block tests give X⪰0. The test D=t·vv^T with v in ker X gives the range condition. D=X^† gives the generalized Schur bound. The completing-the-square step uses X X^† B_j = B_j.
- The extension of the scalar certificate to (z1,z2)=0 by continuity, which is valid because it is a polynomial in z.
- The forward direction via an evaluation functional.
- The dimension count 22·15=330, minus 23 prescribed coordinates, giving 307, and the 20·5=100 moment-matrix size.
sibling_notes: The rank-324 companion paper ("Hyperbolicity Cones Without Semidefinite Lifts") was also reported no_gap_found. This paper uses that companion only for the non-spectrahedrality comparison; the lift proof is self-contained.
